## Why it waits

There is nothing to report an error in. It does not wait one day longer than that: publishing Draft material while offering no way to report what is wrong with it contradicts the reason the material is labelled Draft.

## Definition of Done - additions

- [ ] The report path is documented in `WKF-009` as a route a human actually monitors, with a stated response expectation.
- [ ] The affordance is on the page template, so a new chapter gets it by existing rather than by remembering.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every content page exposes the affordance without per-page configuration.
- [ ] Reporting takes one action from the page where the error was found - no navigation to a separate form to find the page again (`SC-C1`).
- [ ] The report carries the page identity and content version automatically; the reader is never asked to supply what the page already knows (`F-16`).
- [ ] It works with JavaScript disabled, or degrades to a plain link that does.
- [ ] No personal information is required. An anonymous report is a valid report (`TEC-4`).
- [ ] Submitting gives an unambiguous confirmation. Silence after a submit reads as failure and stops the second report.

## Definition of Done - universal

Inherited by every implementation task. `RDM-011` S1 holds the single copy.

- [ ] `pnpm check` passes locally
- [ ] The `CI` status check passes on the pull request (`WKF-004`)
- [ ] Merged by pull request from a branch; never committed to `main` directly
- [ ] Human-written commenting matching the codebase (`WKF-007`)
- [ ] Keyboard reachable, visible focus, correct semantics; no new AA regression (`DSY-011`, `WEB-012`)
- [ ] Both themes; above and below the responsive breakpoints (`WEB-011`, `DSY-010`)
- [ ] The JavaScript budget still holds (`WEB-014` S2)
- [ ] No specification left in conflict with the work (`CST-001`)
- [ ] Decisions recorded (`D-####`); architectural ones get an ADR (`WKF-013`)
